items.title: 14.1.3 Fundamental Mathematical Operations for Vectors in Space (Roman Urdu)

blocks.title: Numbering note
blocks.text: Kitab is heading ko 14.1.4 chhaapti hai (Book# 14.1.4). Kitab mein 14.1.1 naam ki koi heading hai hi nahin, is liye portal 14.1 ke sub-headings ko tarteeb se 14.1.1 se 14.1.8 tak number karta hai. Yahan 14.1.3 wahi hai jo kitab mein 14.1.4 hai.

Ab jab humein pata hai ke space ka har vector \([x, y, z]\) hai, to agla qadam hai un par hisaab karna: jama, tafreeq (minus), scalar se zarb, negative aur barabari. Achhi khabar yeh hai ke sab kuch bilkul plane wale vectors jaisa hai, bas har jagah teesra component bhi saath chalta hai. Chaliye ek ek karke dekhte hain, aur har rule ke saath ek chhota sa number wala misaal bhi.
\(R^{3}\) mein addition aur scalar multiplication hum yun define karte hain:
(i) Addition of vectors: kisi bhi do vectors \(\underline{u} = [x, y, z]\) aur \(\underline{v} = [x', y', z']\) ke liye

blocks.latex: \underline{u} + \underline{v} = [x, y, z] + [x', y', z'] \\ = [x + x',\ y + y',\ z + z']
blocks.text_alt: u plus v equals x plus x prime, y plus y prime, z plus z prime

blocks.text: (ii) Scalar Multiplication of a vector: \(\underline{u} = [x, y, z]\) aur \(a \in R\) ke liye

blocks.latex: a\underline{u} = a[x, y, z] = [ax, ay, az]
blocks.text_alt: a u equals a x, a y, a z

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Bilkul plane jaisa, bas teesra component bhi. Misaal: \(\underline{u} = [1, 2, 3]\), \(\underline{v} = [4, -1, 0]\).
\(\underline{u} + \underline{v} = [1 + 4,\ 2 + (-1),\ 3 + 0] = [5, 1, 3]\)
\(2\underline{u} = [2, 4, 6]\)
\(x'\) mein jo dash hai (parhte hain \"x dash\") woh sirf ek label hai ke yeh doosre vector ka x-component hai; yeh derivative nahin. Isi tarah \(x''\) teesre vector ka x-component hai.
Kyun: component ba component kyun? Kyunke x, y aur z teen alag simtein hain; x ki harkat sirf x ki harkat se judti hai, jaise mashriq wale qadam sirf mashriq walon se.

Real numbers ki saari ordered triples \([x, y, z]\) ka set, jama aur scalar se zarb ke rules ke saath, \(R^{3}\) mein vectors ka set kehlata hai. Vector \(\underline{u} = [x, y, z]\) mein \(x\), \(y\) aur \(z\) ko \(\underline{u}\) ke components kehte hain. \(R^{3}\) mein vectors ki definition yahi kehti hai ke space ke vectors ka jama aur scalar se zarb bhi bilkul waise hi kiya jaaye jaise plane ke vectors ka. Isi tarah hum \(R^{3}\) mein yeh bhi define karte hain:
(a) Vector \(\underline{u} = [x, y, z]\) ka negative:

blocks.text_alt: minus u equals minus one times u equals minus x, minus y, minus z

blocks.text: (b) Do vectors \(\underline{v} = [x', y', z']\) aur \(\underline{w} = [x'', y'', z'']\) ka difference (farq):

blocks.text_alt: v minus w equals v plus minus w equals x prime minus x double prime, and so on

blocks.text: (c) Zero vector:

(d) Equality of two vectors: do vectors \(\underline{v} = [x', y', z']\) aur \(\underline{w} = [x'', y'', z'']\) barabar hain, yani \(\underline{v} = \underline{w}\), tab aur sirf tab jab \(x' = x''\), \(y' = y''\) aur \(z' = z''\).

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab yahan "Tow vectors" chhaapti hai; sahi lafz "Two vectors" hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Kyun: \(\underline{v} - \underline{w}\) ko \(\underline{v} + (-\underline{w})\) kyun likha? Minus ko hum \"ulte vector ko jama karna\" samajhte hain, bilkul jaise numbers mein \(7 - 3 = 7 + (-3)\). Is tarah naya rule yaad nahin karna parta, wahi jama wala rule kaam karta hai.
Zero vector ki lambai sifar hai aur us ki koi khaas simt nahin; yeh numbers mein 0 jaisa hai: kisi bhi vector mein jama karne se kuch nahin badalta.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
(Hamari practice.) \(\underline{v} = [3, 0, 5]\) aur \(\underline{w} = [1, 2, 3]\) lein.
\(-\underline{w} = [-1, -2, -3]\) (har component ka sign badla)
\(\underline{v} - \underline{w} = [3 - 1,\ 0 - 2,\ 5 - 3] = [2, -2, 2]\)
Tasdeeq: \(\underline{w} + (\underline{v} - \underline{w}) = [1 + 2,\ 2 - 2,\ 3 + 2] = [3, 0, 5] = \underline{v}\). Sahi!
Barabari se teen equations: \([a, 2, b + 1] = [3, 2, 5]\) ka matlab \(a = 3\) aur \(b + 1 = 5\), yani \(b = 4\).
(e) Position Vector

\(R^{3}\) ke kisi bhi point \(P(x, y, z)\) ke liye vector \(\underline{u} = [x, y, z]\) ko directed line segment \(\underline{OP}\) se dikhaya jaata hai, jis ka initial point origin par hai. Aise vectors ko \(R^{3}\) mein position vectors (maqaam batane wale vectors) kehte hain, kyunke yeh origin se dekh kar point ki jagah batate hain.
Agar \(A(x_{1}, y_{1}, z_{1})\) aur \(B(x_{2}, y_{2}, z_{2})\) do points hon to \(A\) se \(B\) tak ka vector yeh hai:

blocks.text_alt: vector AB equals OB minus OA
equals x2 minus x1, y2 minus y1, z2 minus z1

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab yahan points \(A(x_{1}, y_{1}, z_{1})\) aur \(B(x'', y'', z'')\) leti hai lekin formula \(\underline{AB} = [x' - x'',\ y' - y'',\ z' - z'']\) chhaapti hai, jis ke numbers in dono points ke hain hi nahin. Sahi qaida \"aakhri point minus shuru ka point\" hai: \(\underline{AB} = [x'' - x_{1},\ y'' - y_{1},\ z'' - z_{1}]\), yani aam naamon ke saath \([x_{2} - x_{1},\ y_{2} - y_{1},\ z_{2} - z_{1}]\). (Yahi baat 14.1.7 mein kitab sahi likhti hai.)

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Kyun: \"aakhri minus shuru\" kyun? \(O\) se \(A\) jaana aur phir \(A\) se \(B\) jaana, seedha \(O\) se \(B\) jaane ke barabar hai: \(\underline{OA} + \underline{AB} = \underline{OB}\). Dono taraf se \(\underline{OA}\) hata dein to \(\underline{AB} = \underline{OB} - \underline{OA}\).
Misaal: \(A(1, 2, 3)\), \(B(4, 0, 5)\): \(\underline{AB} = [4 - 1,\ 0 - 2,\ 5 - 3] = [3, -2, 2]\), aur \(\underline{BA} = [-3, 2, -2]\), bilkul ulta.
Baareek baat: \(\underline{AB}\) khud position vector nahin (yeh \(O\) se shuru nahin hota); yeh \(A\) aur \(B\) ke position vectors se nikalta hai.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text:
\(P(2, -1, 4)\) aur \(Q(5, 3, 4)\) hon to \(\underline{PQ}\) kya hai? Aur \(\underline{QP}\)?
Jawab: \(\underline{PQ} = [5 - 2,\ 3 - (-1),\ 4 - 4] = [3, 4, 0]\); \(\underline{QP} = [-3, -4, 0]\). Dhyan dein: \(3 - (-1) = 4\), minus minus plus ban jaata hai.

Ek misaal se poori baat jor lete hain. Farz karein ek cheel (bird) pehle point \(A(2, 1, 6)\) par thi aur phir point \(B(5, 5, 6)\) par jaa baithi. Us ka displacement vector \(\underline{AB} = [5 - 2,\ 5 - 1,\ 6 - 6] = [3, 4, 0]\) hai. Teesra component sifar hai, matlab unchai nahin badli, cheel ne sirf ufqi (horizontal) safar kiya. Dekha aap ne, components sirf numbers nahin, har ek apni simt ki kahani batata hai. Aage 14.1.4 mein hum isi vector ki lambai bhi nikalna seekhenge.

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
Jama, tafreeq aur scalar se zarb component ba component.
\(-\underline{u} = [-x, -y, -z]\); \(\underline{0} = [0, 0, 0]\).
Do vectors tabhi barabar hain jab teenon components barabar hon.
Point \(P\) ka position vector: \(\underline{OP} = [x, y, z]\).
\(\underline{AB} = \underline{OB} - \underline{OA}\): aakhri minus shuru.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
Ulti tarteeb se minus karna: \(\underline{AB}\) mein \(B - A\) hota hai, \(A - B\) nahin.
\(-\underline{w}\) mein har sign na badalna: \(-[1, -2, 3] = [-1, 2, -3]\).
Scalar se sirf pehla component zarb karna: \(2[1, 2, 3] = [2, 4, 6]\), \([2, 2, 3]\) nahin.
Negative number minus karte waqt sign bhool jaana: \(3 - (-1) = 4\), 2 nahin.
